atomic_tests.name: System Service Discovery
atomic_tests.description:
Identify system services.

Upon successful execution, cmd.exe will execute service commands with expected result to stdout.

executor.name: command_prompt
executor.command:
tasklist.exe /svc
sc query
sc query state= all

atomic_tests.name: System Service Discovery - net.exe
atomic_tests.description:
Enumerates started system services using net.exe and writes them to a file. This technique has been used by multiple threat actors.

Upon successful execution, net.exe will run from cmd.exe that queries services. Expected output is to a txt file in in the temp directory called service-list.txt.

output_file.description: Path of file to hold net.exe output

executor.name: bash
executor.command: if [ "$(uname)" = 'FreeBSD' ]; then service -e; else systemctl --type=service; fi;

atomic_tests.name: Get-Service Execution
atomic_tests.description: Executes the Get-Service cmdlet to gather objects representing all services on the local system.

atomic_tests.name: System Service Discovery - macOS launchctl
atomic_tests.description:
Enumerates services on macOS using launchctl. Used by adversaries for
identifying daemons, background services, and persistence mechanisms.

atomic_tests.name: System Service Discovery - Windows Scheduled Tasks (schtasks)
atomic_tests.description: Enumerates scheduled tasks on Windows using schtasks.exe.

atomic_tests.name: System Service Discovery - Services Registry Enumeration
atomic_tests.description:
Enumerates Windows services by reading the Services registry key
(HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services) instead of using Service Control
Manager APIs or CLI tools such as sc.exe or Get-Service.

executor.name: powershell

atomic_tests.name: System Service Discovery - Linux init scripts
atomic_tests.description:
Enumerates system services by listing SysV init scripts and runlevel
symlinks under /etc/init.d and /etc/rc*.d.

executor.name: sh
executor.command:
echo "[*] Listing SysV init scripts (/etc/init.d):"
if [ -d /etc/init.d ]; then ls -l /etc/init.d; else echo "/etc/init.d not present on this system"; fi
echo
echo "[*] Listing runlevel directories (/etc/rc*.d):"
ls -ld /etc/rc*.d 2>/dev/null || echo "No /etc/rc*.d directories found"
